instructions: Put a 10 inch cast iron skillet in the oven and heat the oven to 425°F with the skillet inside.
Meanwhile, melt 8 tbsp of the butter in a small pan over low heat or in the microwave. Set it aside to cool a little.
In a large bowl, whisk together the 3/4 cup cornmeal, 1 1/2 cups flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1/2 cup sugar and 1/4 tsp salt.
In a second bowl, whisk the 2 eggs. Add 1 cup of the creamed corn, the 3/4 cup milk and the melted butter, and whisk until it's evenly mixed.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix and stir with a spatula until there's no dry flour left. A few lumps are fine. Stop there, or the cornbread comes out tough.

Using oven mitts, take the skillet out of the oven and set it on the stove. Add the last 2 tbsp butter and swirl it around so it coats the bottom and halfway up the sides. The handle is very hot, so keep a mitt on it.
Pour the batter into the skillet and smooth the top. Put it back in the oven and turn the oven down to 375°F.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is light golden and a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean. The top should spring back when you press it.
Leave it in the skillet for 15 minutes, then turn it out onto a board and cut it into 10 wedges. This makes 10 wedges.
method_notes: All three are quick breads that stir a wet mix into flour, cornmeal, sugar and baking powder just until combined. RecipeTin Eats adds a cup of canned creamed corn for moisture, heats a buttered cast iron skillet at 425°F before the batter goes in, then bakes at 375°F for 25 to 30 minutes. Bless This Mess and Dinners, Dishes and Desserts use equal flour and cornmeal with oil or butter and milk, baked at 400°F in a round pan for 20 to 25 minutes, and are sweeter. This follows RecipeTin Eats as written; it makes one 10 inch skillet, about 10 wedges.
